o: Cómo Lázaro se asentó con un fraile de la Merced, y de lo que le acaeció con él.
t: How Lazarillo settled with a Mercedarian friar, and what befell him with him.

o: Hube de buscar el cuarto, y éste fue un fraile de la Merced, que las mujercillas que digo me encaminaron, al cual ellas le llamaban pariente: gran enemigo del coro y de comer en el convento, perdido por andar fuera, amicísimo de negocios seglares y visitar, tanto que pienso que rompía él más zapatos que todo el convento.
t: I had to look for a fourth, and this was a Mercedarian friar, whom the little women I mentioned directed me to, and whom they called a relative: a great enemy of the choir and of eating in the convent, lost to being out and about, a great friend of worldly business and visiting, so that I think he wore out more shoes than the whole convent.

o: Éste me dio los primeros zapatos que rompí en mi vida, mas no me duraron ocho días, ni yo pude con su trote durar más.
t: This man gave me the first shoes I wore out in my life, but they did not last me eight days, nor could I keep up with his trot for longer.

o: Y por esto y por otras cosillas que no digo, salí dél.
t: And because of this and other little things I do not mention, I left him.

o: Cómo Lázaro se asentó con un buldero, y de las cosas que con él pasó.
t: How Lazarillo settled with a bull-leader, and what happened with him.

o: En el quinto por mi ventura di, que fue un buldero, el más desenvuelto y desvengonzado y el mayor echador dellas que jamás yo vi ni ver espero ni pienso que nadie vio; porque tenía y buscaba modos y maneras y muy sotiles invenciones.
t: In the fifth, by my good fortune, I found, that was a bull-leader, the most unbuttoned and shameless and the greatest thrower of them all that I ever saw, nor do I hope to see, nor think anyone ever saw; because he had and sought out ways and manners and very subtle inventions.

o: En entrando en los lugares do habían de presentar la bula, primero presentaba a los clérigos o curas algunas cosillas, no tampoco de mucho valor ni substancia: una lechuga murciana, si era por el tiempo, un par de limas o naranjas, un melocotón, un par de duraznos, cada sendas peras verdiniales.
t: On entering the places where they were to present the bull, he first presented to the clerics or priests some little things, not of much value or substance either: a Murcian lettuce, if it was the season, a pair of limes or oranges, a peach, a pair of apricots, now and then green pears.

o: Ansí procuraba tenerlos propicios porque favoreciesen su negocio y llamasen sus feligreses a tomar la bula.
t: Thus he sought to keep them favorable so that they would favor his business and call his parishioners to take the bull.

o: Ofreciéndosele a él las gracias, informábase de la suficiencia dellos.
t: When they thanked him, he would inquire into their means.

o: Si decían que entendían, no hablaba palabra en latín por no dar tropezón; mas aprovechábase de un gentil y bien cortado romance y desenvoltísima lengua.
t: When they said they understood, he did not speak a word of Latin for fear of stumbling; but he made use of a neat and well-turned romance and a very free and easy tongue.

o: Y si sabía que los dichos clérigos eran de los reverendos, digo que más con dineros que con letras y con reverendas se ordena, hacíase entre ellos un Santo Tomás y hablaba dos horas en latín: a lo menos, que lo parecía aunque no lo era.
t: And if he knew that the said clerics were among the reverends, I say that he was more given to money than to letters, and with reverend men he was at his ease: among them he became a Saint Thomas and spoke two hours in Latin — at least, it seemed so, though it was not.

o: Cuando por bien no le tomaban las bulas, buscaba cómo por mal se las tomasen, y para aquello hacía molestias al pueblo e otras veces con mañosos artificios.
t: When they would not take his bulls by fair means, he sought how they might take them by foul, and to that end he made trouble for the people and sometimes by cunning devices.

o: Y porque todos los que le veía hacer sería largo de contar, diré uno muy sotil y donoso, con el cual probaré bien su suficiencia.
t: And because everything he was seen to do would take long to tell, I will tell of one very subtle and clever one, with which I shall prove his worthiness well.

o: En un lugar de la Sagra de Toledo había predicado dos o tres días, haciendo sus acostumbradas diligencias, y no le habían tomado bula, ni a mi ver tenían intención de se la tomar.
t: In a place in the Sagra of Toledo he had preached two or three days, making his usual efforts, and they had not taken his bull, nor, to my mind, had any intention of taking it from him.

o: Estaba dado al diablo con aquello y, pensando qué hacer, se acordó de convidar al pueblo, para otro día de mañana despedir la bula.
t: He was possessed by the devil over that matter and, thinking what to do, he resolved to invite the people, so that the next morning they would take the bull and send him off.

o: Y esa noche, después de cenar, pusiéronse a jugar la colación él y el alguacil, y sobre el juego vinieron a reñir y a haber malas palabras.
t: And that night, after supper, he and the constable sat down to play a game of cards, and over the game they fell to quarrelling and exchanging foul words.

o: Él llamó al alguacil ladrón, y el otro a él falsario.
t: He called the constable a thief, and the other called him a forger.

o: Sobre esto, el señor comisario mi señor tomó un lanzón que en el portal do jugaban estaba.
t: Upon this, the lord commissioner, my master, took up a lance that was in the porch where they were playing.

o: El aguacil puso mano a su espada, que en la cinta tenía.
t: The constable put his hand to his sword, which he wore at his belt.

o: Al ruido y voces y que todos dimos, acuden los huéspedes y vecinos y métense en medio, y ellos muy enojados procurándose desembarazar de los que en medio estaban, para se matar.
t: At the noise and the shouting, and when we all gave out, the guests and neighbours came running and thrust themselves in between, and the two, very angry, strove to free themselves from those who stood between them so as to kill one another.

o: Mas como la gente al gran ruido cargase y la casa estuviese llena della, viendo que no podían afrentarse con las armas, decíanse palabras injuriosas, entre las cuales el alguacil dijo a mi amo que era falsario y las bulas que predicaba que eran falsas.
t: But since the people crowded in at the great uproar and the house was full of them, seeing that they could not come to blows with weapons, they began to hurl insults at one another, among which the constable said to my master that he was a forger and that the bulls he preached were false.

o: Finalmente, que los del pueblo, viendo que no bastaban a ponellos en paz, acordaron de llevar el alguacil de la posada a otra parte.
t: In the end, the people of the village, seeing that they were not enough to set the two of them at peace, agreed to take the constable away from the inn to another place.

o: Y así quedó mi amo muy enojado; y después que los huéspedes y vecinos le hubieron rogado que perdiese el enojo y se fuese a dormir, se fue.
t: And so my master was left very angry; and after the guests and neighbours had begged him to forgive his anger and go off to bed, he went.

o: Y así nos echamos todos.
t: And so we all went to bed.

o: La mañana venida, mi amo se fue a la iglesia y mandó tañer a misa y al sermón para despedir la bula.
t: Morning having come, my master went to the church and ordered the bell to be rung for Mass and the sermon, so as to take his leave of the bull.

o: Y el pueblo se juntó, el cual andaba murmurando de las bulas, diciendo como eran falsas y que el mesmo alguacil riñendo lo había descubierto; de manera que tras que tenían mala gana de tomalla, con aquello de todo la aborrecieron.
t: And the people gathered, going about muttering over the bulls, saying how they were false and how the constable himself had discovered it in the quarrel; so that, besides their already ill will to take it, they came to abhor it entirely because of all that.

o: El señor comisario se subió al púlpito y comienza su sermón, y a animar la gente a que no quedasen sin tanto bien e indulgencia como la santa bula traía.
t: The lord commissioner mounted the pulpit and began his sermon, urging the people not to be left without so much good and indulgence as the holy bull brought.

o: Estando en lo mejor del sermón, entra por la puerta de la iglesia el alguacil y, desque hizo oración, levantóse y con voz alta y pausada cuerdamente comenzó a decir.
t: While he was at the height of the sermon, the constable came in through the church door and, having made his prayer, rose up and with a loud, slow, steady voice began to say:

o: "Buenos hombres, oídme una palabra, que después oiréis a quien quisiéredes.
t: "Good men, hear me a word, and afterwards you will hear whomever you please.

o: Yo vine aquí con este echacuervo que os predica, el cual engañó y dijo que le favoreciese en este negocio y que partiríamos la ganancia.
t: I came here with this scoundrel who preaches to you, who deceived me and said he would favor me in this business and that we would split the profit.

o: Y acabó su razonamiento.
t: And he ended his reasoning.

o: Algunos hombres honrados que allí estaban se quisieron levantar y echar el alguacil fuera de la iglesia, por evitar escándalo.
t: Some honest men who were there wanted to stand up and throw the constable out of the church, to avoid a scandal.

o: Mas mi amo les fue a la mano y mandó a todos que so pena de excomunión no le estorbasen, mas que le dejasen decir todo lo que quisiese.
t: But my master went up to them and ordered everyone, on pain of excommunication, not to hinder him, but to let him say whatever he wished.

o: Y ansí, él también tuvo silencio, mientras el alguacil dijo todo lo que he dicho.
t: And so he too was silent, while the constable said all that I have told you.

o: Como calló, mi amo le preguntó, si quería decir más, que lo dijese. El alguacil dijo.
t: When he fell silent, my master asked him whether he wanted to say more, and told him to say it. The constable said:

o: "Harto hay más que decir de vos y de vuestra falsedad, mas por agora basta."
t: "There is plenty more to be said about you and your falseness, but for now this is enough."

o: El señor comisario se hincó de rodillas en el púlpito y, puestas las manos y mirando al cielo, dijo ansí.
t: The lord commissary knelt down in the pulpit, laid his hands together, and looking up to heaven, spoke thus:

o: "Señor Dios, a quien ninguna cosa es escondida, antes todas manifiestas, y a quien nada es imposible, antes todo posible, tú sabes la verdad y cuán injustamente yo soy afrentado.
t: "Lord God, to whom nothing is hidden, but everything is manifest, and to whom nothing is impossible, but everything is possible, you know the truth and how unjustly I am being put to shame.

o: En lo que a mí toca, yo lo perdono porque tú, Señor, me perdones.
t: As for what concerns me, I forgive it, because you, Lord, forgive me.

o: No mires a aquél que no sabe lo que hace ni dice; mas la injuria a ti hecha, te suplico, y por justicia te pido, no disimules; porque alguno que está aquí, que por ventura pensó tomar aquesta santa bula, dando crédito a las falsas palabras de aquel hombre, lo dejará de hacer.
t: Do not look upon him who knows not what he does nor says; but the injury done to you, I beseech you, and for justice I ask you, do not dissemble; for someone here who perhaps thought of taking this holy bull, giving credit to the false words of that man, will leave off doing so.

o: Y pues es tanto perjuicio del prójimo, te suplico yo, Señor, no lo disimules, mas luego muestra aquí milagro, y sea desta manera: que si es verdad lo que aquél dice y que traigo maldad y falsedad, este púlpito se hunda conmigo y meta siete estados debajo de tierra, do él ni yo jamás parezcamos.
t: And since it is so great a harm to one's neighbor, I beseech you, Lord, not to dissemble, but rather show here a miracle, and let it be in this manner: that if what that man says is true, and I bring forward wickedness and falseness, let this pulpit sink with me and swallow seven states of earth, so that neither he nor I ever appear again.

o: Y si es verdad lo que yo digo y aquél, persuadido del demonio, por quitar y privar a los que están presentes de tan gran bien, dice maldad, también sea castigado y de todos conocida su malicia."
t: And if what I say is true, and that man, persuaded by the devil, in order to rob and deprive those present of so great a good, speaks evil, let him also be punished and let his malice be known to all."

o: Apenas había acabado su oración el devoto señor mío, cuando el negro alguacil cae de su estado y da tan gran golpe en el suelo que la iglesia toda hizo resonar, y comenzó a bramar y echar espumajos por la boca y torcella, y hacer visajes con el gesto, dando de pie y de mano, revolviéndose por aquel suelo a una parte y a otra.
t: Scarcely had my devout lord finished his prayer, when the black constable fell from his seat and gave such a blow on the ground that the whole church echoed, and began to roar and foam at the mouth, twisting his face and making grimaces, kicking and flailing, rolling over that floor now on one side and now on the other.

o: El estruendo y voces de la gente era tan grande, que no se oían unos a otros.
t: The uproar and cries of the people were so great that they could not hear one another.

o: Algunos estaban espantados y temerosos. Unos decían.
t: Some were terrified and frightened. Some said:

o: "El Señor le socorra y valga."
t: "May the Lord help him and give him strength."

o: "Bien se le emplea, pues levantaba tan falso testimonio."
t: "He is well served, for he was bearing false witness."

o: Finalmente, algunos que allí estaban, y a mi parecer no sin harto temor, se llegaron y le trabaron de los brazos, con los cuales daba fuertes puñadas a los que cerca dél estaban.
t: Finally, some who were there, and in my opinion not without great fear, came up and seized him by the arms, with which he was dealing heavy blows at those near him.

o: Otros le tiraban por las piernas y tuvieron reciamente, porque no había mula falsa en el mundo que tan recias coces tirase.
t: Others pulled at his legs and kicked him lustily, for there was no ill-bred mule in the world that kicked so hard.

o: Y así le tuvieron un gran rato, porque más de quince hombres estaban sobre él, y a todos daba las manos llenas, y si se descuidaban, en los hocicos.
t: And so they had him for a good while, because more than fifteen men were on top of him, and everyone got a fistful, and if they were careless, right in the snouts.

o: A todo esto, el señor mi amo estaba en el púlpito de rodillas, las manos y los ojos puestos en el cielo, transportado en la divina esencia, que el planto y ruido y voces que en la iglesia había no eran parte para apartalle de su divina contemplación.
t: All this while, my lord the master was kneeling in the pulpit, hands and eyes lifted to heaven, carried off into the divine essence, so that the wailing and noise and voices in the church were no part able to draw him away from his divine contemplation.

o: El señor comisario, como quien despierta de un dulce sueño, los miró y miró al delincuente y a todos los que alderredor estaban, y muy pausadamente les dijo.
t: The lord constable, like one waking from a sweet sleep, looked at them and looked at the offender and at everyone standing around, and very slowly he said to them:

o: "Buenos hombres, vosotros nunca habíades de rogar por un hombre en quien Dios tan señaladamente se ha señalado; mas pues él nos manda que no volvamos mal por mal y perdonemos las injurias, con confianza podremos suplicarle que cumpla lo que nos manda, y Su Majestad perdone a éste que le ofendió poniendo en su santa fe obstáculo.
t: "Good men, you never had to pray for a man in whom God has so manifestly set His mark; but since He commands us not to return evil for evil and to forgive injuries, we may confidently beseech Him to fulfill what He commands us, and may His Majesty forgive this one who offended Him by placing an obstacle in His holy faith.

o: Vamos todos a suplicalle."
t: Let us all beseech Him."

o: Y así bajó del púlpito y encomendó a que muy devotamente suplicasen a Nuestro Señor tuviese por bien de perdonar a aquel pecador, y volverle en su salud y sano juicio, y lanzar dél el demonio, si Su Majestad había permitido que por su gran pecado en él entrase.
t: And so he came down from the pulpit and charged them to very devoutly beseech Our Lord to be pleased to forgive that sinner, and restore him to his health and sound judgment, and cast out of him the devil, if His Majesty had permitted that through his great sin the devil had entered in him.

o: Todos se hincaron de rodillas, y delante del altar con los clérigos comenzaban a cantar con voz baja una letanía.
t: Everyone knelt down, and before the altar, together with the clergy, they began to sing a litany in a low voice.

o: Y esto hecho, mandó traer la bula y púsosela en la cabeza; y luego el pecador del alguacil comenzó poco a poco a estar mejor y tornar en sí.
t: And this done, he ordered the bull to be brought and placed it on his head; and then the sinner began little by little to mend and to come to his senses.

o: Y desque fue bien vuelto en su acuerdo, echóse a los pies del señor comisario y demandóle perdón, y confesó haber dicho aquello por la boca y mandamiento del demonio, lo uno por hacer a él daño y vengarse del enojo, lo otro y más principal, porque el demonio recibía mucha pena del bien que allí se hiciera en tomar la bula.
t: And once he was well come to his right mind, he threw himself at the feet of the lord constable and asked his pardon, and he confessed that he had said those things by the mouth and command of the devil, partly to do him harm and avenge his anger, and partly and above all because the devil suffered much from the good that was done there in taking the bull.

o: El señor mi amo le perdonó, y fueron hechas las amistades entre ellos; y a tomar la bula hubo tanta priesa, que casi ánima viviente en el lugar no quedó sin ella: marido y mujer, e hijos e hijas, mozos y mozas.
t: My lord the master forgave him, and they made peace with one another; and there was such a rush to take the bull that scarcely a living soul in the place was left without one: husband and wife, sons and daughters, boys and girls.

o: Divulgóse la nueva de lo acaecido por los lugares comarcanos, y cuando a ellos llegábamos, no era menester sermón ni ir a la iglesia, que a la posada la venían a tomar como si fueran peras que se dieran de balde.
t: The news of what had happened spread through the surrounding villages, and when it reached them there was no need of a sermon or of going to church, for they came to the inn to take it as if it were pears given away for nothing.

o: De manera que en diez o doce lugares de aquellos alderredores donde fuimos, echó el señor mi amo otras tantas mil bulas sin predicar sermón.
t: So that in ten or twelve of those places around where we went, my lord the master dispatched as many thousands of bulls without preaching a sermon.

o: Visto por el asunto de mi amo lo que pasaba y que, aunque decía se fiaban por un año, no aprovechaba y que estaban tan rebeldes en tomarla y que su trabajo era perdido, hizo tocar las campanas para despedirse.
t: Having seen by the business of my master what was going on, and that although they said they would be satisfied for a year, it was of no use, and that they were so rebellious in taking it and that his labor was wasted, he had the bells rung to bid farewell.

o: "Hermanos míos, tomad, tomad de las gracias que Dios os envía hasta vuestras casas, y no os duela, pues es obra tan pía la redención de los captivos cristianos que están en tierra de moros.
t: "My brothers, take, take the graces that God sends you all the way to your houses, and let it not grieve you, for the redemption of Christian captives who are in the land of the Moors is such a pious work.

o: Porque no renieguen nuestra santa fe y vayan a las penas del infierno, siquiera ayudadles con vuestra limosna y con cinco paternostres y cinco avemarías, para que salgan de cautiverio.
t: So that they do not renounce our holy faith and go to the punishments of hell, at least help them with your alms and with five Our Fathers and five Hail Marys, so that they may come out of captivity.

o: Y aun también aprovechan para los padres y hermanos y deudos que tenéis en el Purgatorio, como lo veréis en esta santa bula."
t: And they also avail for the fathers and brothers and kinsmen you have in Purgatory, as you shall see in this holy bull."

o: Como el pueblo las vio ansí arrojar, como cosa que se daba de balde y ser venida de la mano de Dios, tomaban a más tomar, aun para los niños de la cuna y para todos sus defuntos, contando desde los hijos hasta el menor criado que tenían, contándolos por los dedos.
t: When the people saw them thrown out that way, as a thing given away for nothing and come from the hand of God, they took one after another, even for the children in the cradle and for all their dead, counting from the sons to the youngest servant they had, counting them on their fingers.

o: Vímonos en tanta priesa, que a mí aínas me acabaran de romper un pobre y viejo sayo que traía, de manera que certifico a V.M. que en poco más de una hora no quedó bula en las alforjas, y fue necesario ir a la posada por más.
t: We found ourselves in such a press that they nearly finished off a poor old cloak I was wearing, so I certify to Your Majesty that in a little over an hour there was no bull left in the saddlebags, and it was necessary to go to the inn for more.

o: Acabados de tomar todos, dijo mi amo desde el púlpito a su escribano y al del concejo que se levantasen y, para que se supiese quién eran los que habían de gozar de la santa indulgencia y perdones de la santa bula y para que él diese buena cuenta a quien le había enviado, se escribiesen.
t: When all had taken them, my master said from the pulpit to his clerk and to the town's clerk that they should stand up, and that, so that it might be known who were the ones who were to enjoy the holy indulgence and the pardons of the holy bull, and so that he might give a good account to the one who had sent him, they should write them down.

o: Y así luego todos de muy buena voluntad decían las que habían tomado, contando por orden los hijos y criados y defuntos.
t: And so at once, all of them with very good will, gave the names of those they had taken, listing in order the sons, the servants and the dead.

o: Hecho su inventario, pidió a los alcaldes que por caridad, porque él tenía que hacer en otra parte, mandasen al escribano le diese autoridad del inventario y memoria de las que allí quedaban, que, según decía el escribano, eran más de dos mil.
t: Having made his inventory, he asked the mayors, for charity's sake, since he had business elsewhere, to send the notary and have him grant authority for the inventory and a record of the items that remained there, which, according to the notary, came to more than two thousand.

o: E ansí nos partimos, yendo todos muy alegres del buen negocio.
t: And so we parted, all of us very happy over the good business.

o: Decía mi amo al alguacil y escribano.
t: My master said to the constable and the notary.

o: "¿Qué os parece, como a estos villanos, que con solo decir »Cristianos viejos somos», sin hacer obras de caridad, se piensan salvar sin poner nada de su hacienda?
t: "What do you think, you rogues, that by merely saying 'we are old Christians,' without doing any works of charity, they think they can save themselves without putting up any of their money?"

o: Pues, por vida del licenciado Pascasio Gómez, que a su costa se saquen más de diez cautivos."
t: Well, by the life of the licentiate Pascasio Gómez, let more than ten captives be taken at his own expense."

o: Y ansí nos fuimos hasta otro lugar de aquel cabo de Toledo, hacia la Mancha, que se dice, adonde topamos otros más obtinados en tomar bulas.
t: And so we went on to another place on that point of Toledo toward La Mancha, as they say, where we found others even more obstinate in taking bulls.

o: Hechas mi amo y los demás que íbamos nuestras diligencias, en dos fiestas que allí estuvimos no se habían echado treinta bulas.
t: My master and the rest of us having done our diligence, in the two feasts we spent there, thirty bulls had not been let off.

o: Y, ya que hubo acabado la misa y echada la bendición, tomóla con un pañizuelo, bien envuelta la cruz en la mano derecha y en la otra la bula, y ansí se bajó hasta la postrera grada del altar, adonde hizo que besaba la cruz, e hizo señal que viniesen adorar la cruz.
t: And when the mass was over and the blessing had been given, he took it with a handkerchief, the cross well wrapped in his right hand and the bull in the other, and so he came down to the lowest step of the altar, where he made them kiss the cross, and gave the sign for them to come and worship the cross.

o: Y ansí vinieron los alcaldes los primeros y los más ancianos del lugar, viniendo uno a uno como se usa.
t: And so the mayors came first, the oldest men of the place, one by one as is the custom.

o: Y el primero que llegó, que era un alcalde viejo, aunque él le dio a besar la cruz bien delicadamente, se abrasó los rostros y se quitó presto afuera.
t: And the first one who came up, who was an old mayor, though he let him kiss the cross very delicately, screwed up his face and quickly stepped outside.

o: Lo cual visto por mi amo, le dijo.
t: Which, seen by my master, he said to him.

o: "¡Paso, quedo, señor alcalde! ¡Milagro!"
t: "Hold still, sir mayor! A miracle!"

o: Y ansí hicieron otros siete o ocho, y a todos les decía.
t: And so seven or eight others did, and to all of them he said.

o: "¡Paso, señores! ¡Milagro!"
t: "Hold still, gentlemen! A miracle!"

o: Cuando él vido que los rostriquemados bastaban para testigos del milagro, no la quiso dar más a besar.
t: When he saw that the wry faces were enough as witnesses of the miracle, he would not let them kiss it any more.

o: Subióse al pie del altar y de allí decía cosas maravillosas, diciendo que por la poca caridad que había en ellos había Dios permitido aquel milagro y que aquella cruz había de ser llevada a la santa iglesia mayor de su Obispado; que por la poca caridad que en el pueblo había, la cruz ardía.
t: He climbed up to the foot of the altar and from there he said wonderful things, telling them that because of the little charity there was among them God had permitted that miracle, and that that cross was to be carried to the holy cathedral church of his bishopric; that because of the little charity in the town, the cross was burning.

o: Fue tanta la prisa que hubo en el tomar de la bula, que no bastaban dos escribanos ni los clérigos ni sacristanes a escribir.
t: Such was the rush to get the bull that two notaries were not enough, nor the clerics nor the sacristans, to write them down.

o: Creo de cierto que se tomaron más de tres mil bulas, como tengo dicho a V.M. Después, al partir, él fue con gran reverencia, como es razón, a tomar la santa cruz, diciendo que la había de hacer engastonar en oro, como era razón.
t: I am certain that more than three thousand bulls were taken, as I have told Your Majesty. Afterward, at the parting, he went with great reverence, as is fitting, to take the holy cross, saying that he would have it set in gold, as was fitting.

o: Fue rogado mucho del concejo y clérigos del lugar les dejase allí aquella santa cruz por memoria del milagro allí acaecido.
t: He was much entreated by the council and the clerics of the place to leave that holy cross there in memory of the miracle that had happened there.

o: Él en ninguna manera lo quería hacer y al fin, rogado de tantos, se la dejó; con que le dieron otra cruz vieja que tenían antigua de plata, que podrá pesar dos o tres libras, según decían.
t: He in no way wanted to do so, and at last, entreated by so many, he left it with them; whereupon they gave him another old cross they had, an ancient one of silver, which might weigh two or three pounds, as they said.

o: Y ansí nos partimos alegres con el buen trueque y con haber negociado bien.
t: And so we parted happily, with the good bargain and with having negotiated well.

o: En todo no vio nadie lo susodicho sino yo, porque me subía par del altar para ver si había quedado algo en las ampollas, para ponello en cobro, como otras veces yo lo tenía de costumbre.
t: And no one saw what has been told above except me, because I climbed up by the altar to see if anything had been left in the ampullas, to claim it, as I was accustomed to do.

o: Y como allí me vio, púsose el dedo en la boca haciéndome señal que callase.
t: And when he saw me there, he put his finger to his mouth, making me a sign to be quiet.

o: Yo ansí lo hice porque me cumplía, aunque, después que vi el milagro, no cabía en mí por echallo fuera, sino que el temor de mi astuto amo no me lo dejaba comunicar con nadie, ni nunca de mí salió, porque me tomó juramento que no descubriese el milagro.
t: And so I did, because it served me; though after I saw the miracle I could hardly keep it in, for the fear of my cunning master would not let me tell anyone, and it never came out of me at all, because he made me swear that I would not reveal the miracle.

o: Y ansí lo hice hasta agora}.
t: And so I have done up to now.

o: Y aunque mochacho, cayóme mucho en gracia, y dije entre mí.
t: And though he was only a lad, he fell greatly in my favor, and I said to myself:

o: "¡Cuántas destas deben hacer estos burladores entre la inocente gente!"
t: "How many of these things must these tricksters be doing among the innocent folk!"

o: Finalmente, estuve con este mi quinto amo cerca de cuatro meses, en los cuales pasé también hartas fatigas{, aunque me daba bien de comer a costa de los curas y otros clérigos do iba a predicar.}.
t: In the end I stayed with this my fifth master about four months, and in that time I also passed many hardships, though I ate well at the expense of the priests and other clerics wherever I went to preach.
